\[
\begin{gathered}
D(x,y) = I(x,y) - (G_{\sigma} \star I)(x,y),
\\[4pt]
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) =
\begin{cases}
I(x,y) + a\, D(x,y) & \text{if } \lvert D(x,y) \rvert \ge t \\
I(x,y) & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\\[4pt]
\sigma = 2, \quad a = 1, \quad t = 0
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value
- \(G_{\sigma}\): Normalized Gaussian kernel with this sigma and radius floor(3 sigma + 0.5)
- \(\star\): Correlation. The Gaussian is symmetric, so it equals convolution.
- \(D\): Detail, the difference between the image and its blur
- \(a\): Amount
- \(t\): Threshold in 8-bit levels

The blur keeps the coarse picture. Subtracting it from the image leaves the detail D. Adding a times D back makes the detail stronger. Where the detail is smaller than the threshold, the pixel keeps its value. With threshold 0 the filter is linear, and the Operator tab shows its single kernel: (1 + a) at the center minus a times the Gaussian kernel.
